tools.name: mcp__Claude_Code_iOS_Simulator__control
tools.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'press_key' presses a hardware key 'count' times: return, delete (backspace), an arrow, select_all, undo or redo (a key also hides the on-screen keyboard); 'set_appearance' switches the device to light or dark mode; 'appearance' says which it is in; 'set_keyboard' shows or hides the on-screen keyboard (it appears only while a text field has focus, and 'press_key' and 'text' hide it again); 'rotate' turns the device a quarter turn left or right ('direction'); take a 'screenshot' after it and tap in that screenshot's frame, however it comes back; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

app_path.description: For 'launch': absolute path (no ~) to the built .app bundle (e.g. /Users/me/Library/Developer/Xcode/DerivedData/MyApp-abc123/Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/MyApp.app).

device.description: Simulator name (e.g. 'iPhone 17 Pro') or UDID. Defaults to the simulator already attached, else the first booted one. The first use of a device asks the user for permission.

udid.description: Alias for 'device' (identical semantics: simulator name or UDID). Pass at most one of 'device' / 'udid'.

bundle_id.description: For 'launch': bundle identifier. If omitted, extracted from the .app's Info.plist.

points.description: For 'touch_path': touch path samples in device points. First point is touch-down; last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

points2.description: For 'touch2_path': two-finger path samples in device points. Each sample carries both contacts (x1/y1, x2/y2); first is touch-down, last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

duration.description: Seconds. For 'tap', >0.5 is a long-press. For 'swipe', the gesture duration (default 0.3).

key.description: For 'press_key': the key or edit command to press.

count.description: For 'press_key': how many times to press it, 1 to 20 (default 1).

state.description: For 'set_keyboard': 'show' or 'hide' the on-screen keyboard. For 'set_appearance': 'light' or 'dark'.

url.description: For 'open_url': URL or scheme to open in the simulator.

tools.name: mcp__terminal__read_terminal

content.content:
<#
    .SYNOPSIS
    Exports the built-in Maester test catalog to JSON for the website test-docs generator.

    .DESCRIPTION
    Imports the Maester module from source (powershell/Maester.psd1), reads every built-in native test
    with Get-MtTest and writes its metadata to a JSON file. website/scripts/generate-test-docs.mjs reads
    that file, plus each test's Test.<ID>.md, to build the test pages of the website.

    Each test has its attributes (Product, RelatedProduct, Feature, Area and ResourceType as taxonomy keys),
    the derived Block, Suite and Source, and LegacyTag: the tags it carried in Maester 2.x, which -Tag still
    matches. Taxonomy at the top level gives the display names of the keys and ATT&CK techniques the tests use.

    A test of a suite that implements a published benchmark also has Benchmark, from the framework file of its
    suite (tests/<suite>/frameworks/<key>.json): Framework, Version, Requirement and the requirement's own
    facts, such as the CIS level and profiles. Its Control lists the controls of other frameworks that the
    requirement relates to. Benchmark is null for every other test. Frameworks at the top level gives the Name,
    Version and Url of each framework by Key.

    No tenant connection is needed and no test code is run. Importing the module requires
    Microsoft.Graph.Authentication to be installed (it is a RequiredModule of Maester).

    The output is deterministic: tests are sorted by ID (ordinal, case-insensitive), paths are
    repository-relative with forward slashes, and the file is UTF-8 without BOM with LF line endings.

    .PARAMETER OutputPath
    Where to write the JSON file. Defaults to website/src/data/test-catalog.json, the catalog the website builds from.

    .EXAMPLE
    ./build/docs/Export-MtTestCatalogForDocs.ps1

    Writes website/src/data/test-catalog.json. The website's build turns it into the test pages; `npm run
    export-catalog` (in website/) runs this script.
#>
[CmdletBinding()]
param(
    [Parameter()]
    [string] $OutputPath
)

## 📑 Description

**Merge after maester365/maester#2679 and maester365/maester#2680.** This branch builds on both, so their commits show here until they are merged.

The test catalog on maester.dev gets the report's way of browsing, showing checks instead of results:

- **Left nav** on every catalog page:
  - Overview, All checks and MITRE ATT&CK.
  - One click to each of the 14 products (with icons and counts), each framework (with its coverage, such as CIS 144/144 or Essential Eight 14/126) and each pack.
  - The suites, which are still at their old URLs.
  - The page's filters: severity, area, effort to fix, impact on users, source (built in or a pack) and channel (new in the preview, `-IncludePreview`).
  - A search box; press `/` to focus it.
- **All checks, a product, a pack or a suite** lists its checks grouped by product, feature, area, severity, suite or pillar, with a severity bar and the `Invoke-Maester` command for the selection. Filters from a link (product, feature, technique, search) show as chips you can remove. All filters are kept in the URL.
  - A product page has its feature tiles.
  - The pack page has its pillar tiles and a notice that Microsoft maintains the checks.
- **Overview** (`/docs/tests/overview`): the product by security area matrix (a cell opens its checks), coverage for each framework and the most defended techniques.
- **Frameworks** (`/docs/tests/frameworks/<key>`): each section and requirement with its checks, the requirements no check covers yet, and filters for level and "No check yet". CIS M365, CIS GitHub, CISA SCuBA, Essential Eight, ISM and NIST SP 800-53.
- **ATT&CK** (`/docs/tests/attack`): techniques by tactic, shaded by the number of checks.
- **Zero Trust Assessment:** its 364 checks are in the catalog, placed under their products by the mapping in #2680. It has a pack page, and each check gets a page with its ratings, where Maester places it, the built-in checks that test the same setting, and links to Microsoft's source. The checks' text lives in Microsoft's module, not in this repository, so those pages link to it.

**How it works**
- `build/docs/Export-MtTestCatalogForDocs.ps1` now also exports the packs that ship with Maester, and builds the taxonomy names from both.
- `website/scripts/catalog-explorer.mjs` writes `src/data/explorer.json` (ignored by git) from the export, the framework files and the NIST list. `generate-test-docs.mjs` calls it and writes the new pages.
- The components are in `website/src/components/catalog/`. The nav and the list share their state through the URL (`state.ts`). `TestCatalog.astro` is removed.
- Every check stays in the page's HTML, so the lists work without JavaScript and search engines see every check.

## ✅ Checks
- [x] My pull request adheres to the code style of this project.
- [ ] My code requires changes to the documentation.
- [ ] I have updated the documentation as required.
- [x] The build and unit tests pass after running `/powershell/tests/pester.ps1` locally. (All 6,865 pass, run with `-Exclude ZeroTrustAssessmentPack*`; that file fails only where the module is installed.)

## ℹ️ Additional Information

- `astro build` succeeds (1,698 pages), and `check-url-contract.mjs` reports all 2,679 old URLs resolve.
- Checked in `npm run dev` at desktop width: All checks with filters, the command and URL, a matrix link and its chips, the Entra ID page with tiles, the Essential Eight page, ATT&CK, the pack page and ZTA.21796. At phone width I checked a product page only.
- Not done yet: the right-hand column on a check page from the design (maps to, defends against, more in this feature). ATT&CK filters on the ATT&CK page.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
EOF

content.text:
The catalog explorer is built and open as [maester365/maester#2682](https://github.com/maester365/maester/pull/2682). It's running at http://localhost:3200/docs/tests if you want to try it.

**What's in it**
- **Left nav** on every Test catalog page:
  - Overview, All checks (1,254) and MITRE ATT&CK.
  - One click to each of the 14 products with icons and counts, each framework with its coverage (CIS 144/144, CISA 76/79, Essential Eight 14/126), and the ZTA pack.
  - The suites, folded away.
  - The page's filters: severity, area, effort, impact, source and channel.
  - A search box; press `/` to jump to it.
- **Lists** (All checks, a product, the pack, a suite) group by product, feature, area, severity, suite or pillar. Each has a severity bar and an `Invoke-Maester` command that follows the filters. Filters live in the URL, so a filtered view can be shared.
  - Product pages have feature tiles.
  - The pack page has pillar tiles and a notice that Microsoft maintains its checks.
- **Overview:** the product × area matrix (each cell opens its checks), coverage for each framework, and the most defended techniques.
- **Framework pages** for CIS M365, CIS GitHub, CISA, Essential Eight, ISM and NIST. Each lists every requirement with its checks, including the ones no check covers yet, with level and "No check yet" filters.
- **ATT&CK page:** techniques by tactic, shaded by how many checks cover them.
- **ZTA in the catalog:** all 364 checks appear in the lists, and each has its own page. A page shows its ratings, its Maester product and area, any built-in check that tests the same setting, and links to Microsoft's source. The description and fix text live only in Microsoft's module, not in this repo, so the pages link to them instead of showing them.

**Checked**
- The production build succeeds with 1,698 pages, and all 2,679 old URLs still resolve.
- Unit tests: 6,865 pass, run without the ZTA pack test file, which fails only on machines with the module installed.
- In the browser at desktop width: All checks with filters, the command and the URL, a matrix link and its chips, the Entra ID page, the Essential Eight page, ATT&CK, the pack page and ZTA.21796.
- At phone width I only checked a product page. That's where I moved the tiles to two per row.

**Merge order:** #2682 includes the commits of [#2679](https://github.com/maester365/maester/pull/2679) and [#2680](https://github.com/maester365/maester/pull/2680). Merge those first, then #2682. All three need a review, and #2682's CI checks haven't started yet.

**Not built yet**
- The right-hand column on a check page from the design: what it maps to, which techniques it defends against, and more checks in the same feature.
- Filters on the ATT&CK page.
